findings.summary: The gate reads only `--configuration runtimeClasspath`, but rule 5's claim is a COMPILE-time one ("compile without Helidon on the classpath"). A `compileOnly` dependency never appears in runtimeClasspath, so any HTTP library declared `compileOnly` in format/binstore-spi/sequencer/ingest is invisible to this gate — including to the exact scenario the file header describes.
findings.failure_scenario: Add to ingest/build.gradle.kts: `dependencies { compileOnly("io.helidon.webserver:helidon-webserver:4.1.1") }`, and add `import io.helidon.webserver.http.ServerRequest;` to an ingest production class. `:ingest:build` compiles green (compileOnly is on compileClasspath and -Werror does not object). `check-module.sh` then resolves runtimeClasspath, sees only `project :binstore-spi / :format / :sequencer`, matches no group, and prints `ok 1 module(s) checked (changed module directories)`. Verified on this tree: adding `compileOnly(libs.assertj.core)` to ingest, `:ingest:dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath` shows only the three project deps, while `--configuration compileClasspath` shows `\--- org.assertj:assertj-core:3.27.3`. Fix: iterate both runtimeClasspath and compileClasspath (and consider testCompileClasspath/testRuntimeClasspath, since a T0 test in `format` starting a Helidon server is also a rule-5 reference), checking exit status and emptiness for each.

findings.summary: HTTP_GROUPS is a hand-maintained denylist, and the header now presents the script as "the gate architecture.md rule 5 has promised". Several mainstream HTTP stacks are not in it, and JDK `java.net.http` needs no coordinate at all, so a green line overstates what was proved.
findings.failure_scenario: Checked against a synthetic runtimeClasspath report: `io.undertow:undertow-core`, `io.vertx:vertx-web`, `org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core`, `com.linecorp.armeria:armeria`, `org.jboss.resteasy:resteasy-core`, `io.projectreactor.netty:reactor-netty-http` and `io.grpc:grpc-netty-shaded` all pass unmatched (note `io.projectreactor.netty` does not contain the substring `io.netty`). Separately, `sequencer` can `import java.net.http.HttpClient` and issue real HTTP with zero declared dependency. Not blocking — a denylist is inherently incomplete — but the success line and header should say "no listed HTTP group" rather than imply rule 5 is fully asserted. The durable form is an allowlist over the catalogue once M0.19 (`check-catalog-only.sh`) forbids literal coordinates.

Restore the index (drop `# probe`) or re-run the round against the new hash.
